note: Rewritten from the original description of Emerson 1925 (English); the original published the species as Rhinotermes (Rhinotermes) longilabius, later placed in Dolichorhinotermes. The checklist gives the year as 1924, while the pages of the original volume (Zoologica 6(4)) are marked 1925. The minor-soldier measurements are abbreviated in the original (e.g. .35) and are given here as 0.35; OCR turned "half" into a two-fraction form, and the distance between the compound eye and the lower margin of the head is transcribed as worded in the original, unchanged.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head brown, yellow around the bases of the antennae; the mandibles have a dark margin; the head is round, with a few scattered long setae, and two large, conspicuous muscle impressions in front of the ocelli. The fontanelle is small and lies on the line joining the two ocelli. The front of the head is raised and meets the base of the clypeus; in front of the fontanelle there are several dark wrinkles sloping backwards and downwards. The antennae are yellow, with 20 segments, segments 2, 3 and 4 about equal in length. The compound eyes are rather large, their lower margin about 2/6 of the compound eye diameter from the lower margin of the head. The ocelli are small, their distance from the compound eye less than their own diameter. The clypeus is yellow, its anterior margin produced and projecting over the labrum, its base relatively broad, with a longitudinal groove along the midline. The pronotum is brown with a pale T-shaped mark in the middle; about as wide as the head, with scattered long setae. The posterior margins of the mesonotum and metanotum are nearly straight. The wings are dark with a reticulate pattern. The abdominal tergites are brown and densely covered with setae; the abdominal sternites are yellow tinged with brown. Measurements: length with wings 8.00—8.50 mm, length without wings 5.50—5.80 mm, head length 1.29—1.50 mm, head width 1.28—1.29 mm, antennal length 2.35 mm, diameter of the compound eye 0.29 mm, pronotum length 0.50—0.59 mm and width 1.06—1.07 mm, forewing length 5.36—5.59 mm and width 1.85—2.00 mm, length of the female 12.50 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major soldier: head yellow, densely covered with setae, widest posteriorly. The antennae are pale, with 16 segments, segment 3 slightly longer than segment 2 or segment 4. The labrum is elongate, reaching almost to the tip of the mandibles, its tip slightly concave. The mandibles are large: the left mandible has 2 large pointed teeth, the second slightly smaller than the first, and near the base a further very small third tooth is visible; the right mandible has 1 large bicuspid tooth (the first cusp anterolateral, the second at the tip of that tooth) and near the base a further extremely small third tooth. The pronotum is yellow and densely covered with long setae; the legs are pale; the abdomen is yellow. Measurements: body length 3.65—4.10 mm, head length 1.65—1.76 mm, head width 1.06—1.10 mm, antennal length 1.53—1.55 mm, pronotum length 0.35—0.38 mm and width 0.65—0.66 mm, hind tibia 0.65—0.76 mm, length of the left mandible 0.70—0.75 mm.
Minor soldier: head, thorax and abdomen yellow; legs and antennae pale; head, thorax and abdomen densely covered with setae. The head is widest behind the antennae, the posterior margin rounded. The labrum is slender and forked at the tip; the mandibles are reduced. The antennae have 14 segments (12 in specimens from young colonies). Measurements: body length 2.35—3.50 mm, head length 1.10—1.12 mm, head width 0.53 mm, distance from the tip of the labrum to the fontanelle 0.53 mm, antennal length 1.28—1.29 mm, hind tibia 0.45—0.59 mm, pronotum length 0.22—0.23 mm and width 0.40—0.41 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The original published the species as Rhinotermes (Rhinotermes) longilabius. The type locality is Kartabo, British Guiana; the holotype is a major soldier and the morphotype an alate; the description is based on specimens of all castes collected by the author from 12 different colonies at Kartabo.
